ANCESTRY.value: Option pricing (Black & Scholes 1973; Merton 1973) and the inverse problem -- implied volatility -- solved to machine precision in two iterations by Peter Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational' (2013/2015), a precision-engineering algorithm (rational approximations per branch, careful handling of extreme moneyness). vollib wraps Jaeckel's reference C++ as Python (py_lets_be_rational is the translation).

cut.note: the inverse of the Black option-pricing formula (given a price, find the volatility) solved to machine precision in a bounded number of steps by Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational': normalise the price, form a rational-cubic first guess whose branches are chosen by regime (near the intrinsic value, near the money, deep out of the money), then take one or two Householder (third-order) steps on a transformed objective so that the iteration count does not depend on the input; py_vollib is the packaging that exposes this under the Black and Black-Scholes-Merton conventions

organs.mechanism: the discounted price is undiscounted and normalised by the forward and strike; the normalised Black price is a monotone function of volatility with known asymptotics at zero and infinity, so a rational-cubic interpolant (a Pade-like guess with regime-selected control points) gives a starting volatility close to the root everywhere; a Householder step (using the first three derivatives of the normalised price, which are cheap closed forms) then converges cubically, so one or two steps reach double precision regardless of moneyness; the limited-iterations entry exposes N so a caller can trade a little accuracy for a fixed cost
organs.input: a price, forward, strike, time, and call/put flag
assumptions: the normalised Black price is monotone and smooth in volatility with analytic derivatives; a good regime-aware first guess makes a fixed small step count enough (Jaeckel 2013/2015)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: implied volatility to machine precision in two iterations, replacing bisection or Newton loops with input-dependent iteration counts
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: prices below the intrinsic value or above the forward have no real volatility; the code has denormalisation/limit branches for those (in the py_lets_be_rational body, not read here)
organs.human_prior: Black 1976; Jaeckel 2013 'Let's Be Rational'; the rational-cubic interpolation is Jaeckel's
organs.source_boundary: the py_vollib wrappers; the numerics are in py_lets_be_rational (not in this tree); MEDIUM accordingly

pressures.condition: an organism inverts a monotone but stiff price-to-volatility map for a stream of quotes spanning deep in, at, and deep out of the money; the score is accuracy and the worst-case iteration count over the stream

pressures.world_punishes: bisection (linear, input-dependent); Newton from a fixed guess (diverges in the wings)
pressures.world_rewards: a regime-aware rational-cubic guess plus a third-order step
pressures.observable_consequence: iterations to double precision vs moneyness for bisection, Newton, and the rational-guess Householder method on a grid of forwards/strikes; error at the intrinsic-value boundary
